title: KV cache slab fragmentation and hash-duplication action plan
creator: Maya Chen
description: Follow-up plan after a production incident where KV prefix cache memory efficiency degraded due to slab allocator fragmentation combined with a hash-duplication bug that caused logical key aliasing. This ticket captures findings, short-term mitigations, and medium-term engineering work to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: On 2026-02-27 we observed sustained elevated eviction rates, tail latency regressions, and increased OOM restarts on a subset of Dedicated pools serving long-lived chat workloads. Root cause analysis found the slab allocator was producing fragmented free space, while a hash-duplication condition in the cache index allowed multiple in-memory entries to reference the same logical prefix bucket, preventing efficient compaction and leading to effective memory exhaustion for hot shards.
impact: Multiple customer routes experienced increased 95th/99th percentile latencies for generation requests. Two Dedicated hosts auto-restarted due to OOMs, triggering failovers and a brief capacity reduction (~8% of affected pool throughput) that caused request queuing and elevated error rates for ~90 minutes during mitigation and rollback.
timeline_summary: 02-27 09:12 Detection: alerts for eviction rate and 99p latency. 02-27 09:35 Mitigation: temporarily reduced batching and enabled aggressive eviction on affected hosts. 02-27 10:10 Rollback: rolled back prior allocator change from runtime-1.21 and removed a recent experimental hash-salting optimization. 02-27 11:45 Recovery: eviction rates and latencies returned to baseline. 03-01 Postmortem kickoff and detailed heap indexing review.
root_cause: Two interacting regressions. 1) Slab allocator change (runtime-1.21) introduced a fragmentation pattern for mixed-size cache entries that prevented in-place reuse of free segments. 2) A separate hash-salting optimization produced nondeterministic hash collisions under certain input distributions which created duplicate logical entries that never reached normal eviction invariants (missing tombstone mark), effectively bypassing eviction accounting and increasing live memory.
detection: Signal came from combined telemetry: eviction_rate, kv_cache_live_bytes, per-host OOM events, and console SLO alerts. On-call attached heap profiles and index snapshots which revealed many small unreachable free ranges and duplicate index entries referencing the same prefix ID.
remediation_completed: Short-term: rolled back the allocator change in runtime-1.21 on affected pools and reverted the hash-salting optimization. Enabled an emergency compaction path that coalesces small free ranges during low-traffic windows. These actions restored memory headroom and reduced eviction storms. Long-term work below is planned.
action_items: A1: Implement deterministic hash stability tests in unit/integration suites to prevent nondeterministic collisions (owner: Arjun, estimate: 2)
A2: Add tombstone and reference-count invariants to cache index; fail-fast on violation in canaries (owner: Priya Ramesh, estimate: 3)
A3: Enhance slab allocator with periodic offline coalescing and a hot/cold bucket rebalancer to avoid fragmentation under mixed-size workloads (owner: Luca Moretti, estimate: 8)
A4: Instrument per-shard fragmentation metrics (free-run-length distribution, largest-free-block, compaction-frequency) and add dashboards/alerts (owner: Elaine Park, estimate: 3)
A5: Create a synthetic soak test harness that injects worst-case prefix distributions to validate compaction and eviction invariants at scale in CI (owner: SRE team, estimate: 5)
A6: Backfill end-to-end canary for allocator and index changes with 72-hour run and automatic rollback on elevated fragmentation or eviction anomalies (owner: Release Engineering, estimate: 3)
A7: Update runbooks to include quick detection and emergency compaction steps plus a checklist for rollback vs live patch (owner: On-call rotation leads, estimate: 1)
A8: Post-deploy review and sign-off gate for any runtime memory allocator or hash algorithm changes (owner: Eng leadership, estimate: 1)
A9: Validate Dedicated pool upgrade process to ensure rolling restarts avoid correlated restarts when compaction runs (owner: Runtime QA, estimate: 2)
A10: Run a retro with product and SRE to evaluate customer communication timelines and improve stakeholder notifications during capacity incidents (owner: Maya Chen, estimate: 1)
A11: Audit other experimental optimizations enabled by default flags to ensure they have safety nets and feature gates (owner: Feature Flagging team, estimate: 2)
followups: F1: Deliver slot-level compaction PR and run against canary fleet (target: 2026-03-18)
F2: Merge index invariants and enable in-simulated mode for two cycles before forcing in prod (target: 2026-04-01)
F3: Complete telemetry dashboard and alerting, then add to on-call checklist (target: 2026-03-22)
F4: Cross-team review with QA and SRE for synthetic soak scenarios (target: 2026-03-30)
notes: This incident highlights a common failure mode when allocator changes and index-level optimizations interact. The probability of recurrence can be materially reduced by (1) stronger pre-merge tests that simulate real prefix distributions, (2) tighter invariants surfaced during canaries, and (3) richer fragmentation telemetry. We should treat any future allocator work as high-risk and gate it behind canary soak windows and automated rollback on fragmentation regression metrics.
